questions.stem:
Statements: All flowers are bright. Some bright things are stars.

Conclusions: I. Some flowers are stars. II. Some bright things are flowers.
questions.explanation: I: Flowers ⊂ Bright; some Bright are Stars — flowers and stars may not overlap. NOT NECESSARILY TRUE. II: All flowers ⊂ bright ⟹ some bright are flowers. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All birds have wings. All wings are useful.

Conclusions: I. All birds are useful. II. Some useful things are birds.
questions.explanation: I: Birds have wings (subset relation) ≠ birds are wings. So 'all wings are useful' doesn't make all birds useful. FALSE. II: Same reason — birds aren't wings. FALSE. Neither follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 14 February 2024 was Wednesday, what day was 14 February 2025?

questions.stem:
Question: Who is the tallest among A, B, C, D?

Statement I: A is taller than B but shorter than C.
Statement II: D is taller than C.
questions.explanation: From I: B < A < C. From II: C < D. Combined: B < A < C < D. So D is tallest. Both together sufficient.

questions.stem: Approximately what % of India's population is under 35, per the passage?
questions.passage_context: Skill development has emerged as a critical component of India's economic strategy. With over 65% of the population under 35, the demographic dividend depends on equipping young Indians with employable skills. Government schemes — Skill India, PMKVY, Apprenticeship Promotion — aim to train tens of millions across diverse sectors. Yet the gap between skill supply and industry demand persists. Many graduates lack practical workplace skills despite formal qualifications. Industries report difficulty filling specialised roles. The new National Education Policy emphasises vocational training from class 6 onward — a long-term structural fix. In parallel, public-private partnerships and industry-aligned curricula are being scaled. The success of these efforts will determine whether India's demographic dividend becomes a productivity advantage or a missed opportunity.
questions.explanation: Stated explicitly: 'over 65% of the population under 35.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) Vande Bharat trains have set new benchmarks.
(B) Indian Railways has undergone major modernisation.
(C) Electrification is now nearly complete on key routes.
(D) High-speed corridors are under planning.
(E) Future plans aim at full electrification by 2030.
questions.explanation: B (intro) → C (electrification) → A (Vande Bharat) → D (corridors) → E (future). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the LAST sentence.

(A) The Internet of Things connects everyday devices.
(B) Smart homes, wearables, and industrial sensors are common examples.
(C) Data privacy and security challenges grow with each new device.
(D) Standards are being developed to address these concerns.
(E) The next decade will see IoT integration become near-universal.
questions.explanation: A (intro) → B (examples) → C (challenges) → D (response) → E (closing). Last = E.
